When I was finishing sixth grade, my younger brother was born and we moved about 40 miles from that parish the next week. I learned that the priest had been sent to Peru where he got a local girl prego and he was defrocked. My younger brother took to riding motorcycles and died by losing an argument with a car splitting lanes on the freeway. I found out in the coroners report that he had type "O" blood. The rest of us kids are all type "B". "A" and "B" are co-dominant over "O". My father never said a word and treated my younger brother like one of his own his whole life. I'm not religious any more and I will not let my father want for anything.

I was backpacking a few years ago with my dad on a point where an old lookout used to be before it fell over off one of the sides that is a cliff into a large bowl shaped mountainside. I went down it on a small trail and started to slide and fell 15 feet and then started rolling down the rocky hillside for a couple hundred feet. Seriously I should've died. I have no idea why I didn't.
I walked away with only a scraped knee and a fractured arm, but seeing my dad at the top of the point kneeling down thinking I just died really got to me. He started crying when I stood up and started climbing back up.

That really changed how I live life, not so much a fear of death but knowing the heartbreak it would be for the people I love to lose me or what it would be like to lose one them. I spend a lot more time with friends and family than before, and a lot more time really caring about them.

I always had stuff done for me growing up which left me with very little life skills. I went to a different country for school and didn't speak the language. As soon as I pulled up in front of my flat, I knew I was in trouble. I wanted to go home immediately but I stuck it out. Things got really bad and I cried every night praying that I would die in my sleep.

It took me forever to get anywhere because I kept getting lost. For a week I only went to school and to the store across the street. Finally I made myself pay attention. I took notes on where I went and managed to have an okay last two weeks. Flying home I was still a mess mentally but a month or so after I got home, I realized that the trip had actually bettered me.

I realized that when push comes to shove, I can do more than I think I can do.

One year ago, my father had a massive heart attack. He barely survived. It was caused by his incredibly obese lifestyle. That was the day I became a shitlord.

I grew up in a fat family. Fat mom, fat dad, fat brother, fat grandparents, fat uncles, fat aunts. While I wasn't ever a jock by any means, I was pretty active. I would bike to my friend's house to play video games and such, so I never got fat. Normally I hated the fitness guys, since they were usually jerks, and I was a nerd that had no interest in sports. I never really thought about weight and just thought "that's the way they are" whenever the topic was raised.

Then my family started dying off and being disabled, and each problem traced back to obesity. Once my dad found out what 98% blockage in his arteries feels like, something clicked in my mind. I have, in the last year, become something of a fitness nut. I decided I never want to be like them, and I don't want them to be like them.

I started encouraging my mom to exercise more and eat healthier, because I don't want her to die at age 55 from what amounts to a slow suicide. I have been hitting a brick wall. The same applies to every other person in my family. When I hear their excuses and fat-logic, it infuriates me, and my only outlet is to work out and exercise myself. As a result, I am now in the best physical condition I have ever been in, and I don't see any sign of slowing down. It feels absolutely amazing.

I decided to enter a scholarship program from my father's company for a year long exchange student program. That experience was a springboard to convince my supervisor that I was the right choice for an expatriate assignment at 23. Now at 41, I'm moving to my 5th country.

Having my arm ripped off, re-attached, then spending 31 days in a hospital quarantine ward with a severe antibiotic resistant staph infection that almost killed me. A month in a 150 sq ft room with mostly people in hazard gear and day after day of "nope that didn't work either..." Daily visits from the Chaplin to see if I wanted to talk, and finally being asked to write a will when they weren't sure if they would be able to get it to respond to any treatment. What can you do? I promised myself I would buy a motorcycle, and go to college (former high school drop out). I bought an older motorcycle a year after I recovered, got my AAS with high honors and am finishing my BA now (honors). Nothing like spending a month not knowing whether you will live or die, getting steadily worse every day, to provide perspective and motivation. I still can't talk to my parents about it, I get so choked up I just can't get the words out. They were out of state and couldn't come visit due to money issues, I downplayed how serious it was to them so they wouldn't worry.

Such is life.
